'''Michael Stumpf''' (born 1970) is a scholar in the field of [[systems biology]], in particular the inference of [[mathematical model]]s using [[statistical inference]] and [[machine learning]] approaches. He has made ample contributions to [[network science]], [[Cell fate determination|cell fate decision making processes]] and [[population genetics]].

==Life==

Stumpf was born in [[Regensburg]], [[Germany]], and grew up in [[Straubing]] and [[Rothenburg ob der Tauber]]. He studied physics at the Universities of [[University of Tübingen|Tübingen]], [[University of Sussex|Sussex]] and [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]]. Upon graduating with his diploma in physics, he went on to study as a graduate student at the [[University of Oxford]], where he received his [[DPhil.]] in statistical physics in 1999. Whilst a graduate student he was a member of [[Balliol College]]. In 1999 Stumpf moved into [[biology]] and worked for three years at the Department of Zoology of the University of Oxford with Professor [[Robert May, Baron May of Oxford]]. During this time Stumpf held a [[fellow]]ship at [[Linacre College]]. Since 2003 Stumpf has worked at the Centre for Bioinformatics at [[Imperial College]], London. In 2004 he was awarded an EMBO Young Investigator Award, and in  2007 Stumpf was appointed to the Chair of Theoretical Systems Biology at [[Imperial College]], London.<ref name="General">{{Cite web|url=http://www.theosysbio.bio.ic.ac.uk/people/michael-stumpf/|title=Theoretical Systems Biology &#124; Michael Stumpf|website=www.theosysbio.bio.ic.ac.uk|accessdate=5 January 2022}}</ref> He has held a [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]], and in 2011 he was awarded the Rector's Medal for Excellence in Research Supervision,<ref name="Rector's Medal">{{cite web |url=http://www.icpress.co.uk/news/11052301.shtml |title=Imperial College Press |accessdate=2011-06-22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110616224758/http://www.icpress.co.uk/news/11052301.shtml |archivedate=2011-06-16 }}</ref> and a Miegunyah Distinguished Fellowship in 2013.

Stumpf is married with two children and lives in [[West (London sub region)|West London]].

In January 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://research.unimelb.edu.au/integrative-genomics/news-and-research-highlights/new-mig-group-leader|title=New MIG Group Leader|date=2018-01-11|website=Melbourne Integrative Genomics (@MelbIntGen)|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-20}}</ref> he moved his research group to the [[University of Melbourne]]. He was elected a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science in May 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Stumpf |url=https://www.science.org.au/profile/michael-stumpf |access-date=2025-05-26 |website=Australian Academy of Science |language=en}}</ref>

==Work==

Stumpf's research covers a variety of fields, including
* development of statistical approaches and methodologies for the integrative analysis of systems biology data.
* statistical and mathematical analysis of complex dynamical systems.
* the analysis of complex biological networks, including [[protein interaction]] and [[Regulation of gene expression|gene regulation]] networks.
* mathematical modelling of molecular, cellular and developmental systems and processes in biology.
